findings.summary: The repair and updated fallback description are accurate for non-default branches, but the unqualified uniqueness claim overstates the guarantee.
evidence: The router returns no token for `main`, `master`, `trunk`, and `develop`; those branches use the shared `followup` naming sequence instead.

The notes say “Distinct branches share a record name only on a hash-prefix collision,” then state that on a default branch or detached HEAD the counter remains. Separate worktrees on distinct default branches can select the same counter-based record name.
findings.action: Qualify the uniqueness claim as applying to non-default branches, and say that the default-branch and detached-HEAD counter can still produce shared names across worktrees.

counterweight_triage.concern: The prior slugless-branch omission in R-003.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes now say that a name whose slug is empty becomes `branch`; the router and test confirm that fallback. The raw-branch hash and prefix-collision caveat are also described.

counterweight_triage.disposition: The packet says the other five selected inputs are unchanged; this review did not reassess those prior dispositions.

next_move: Narrow the uniqueness claim to non-default branches and retain the stated counter behavior for default branches and detached HEADs.
